title: Sprint buffer earmarking and price decay experiment
body:
Purpose: capture a pragmatic, short-window protocol for earmarking a sprint-level capacity buffer (GPU credits / reserved tokens) and an associated temporary surcharge model that decays across the sprint to smooth demand spikes without immediate hiring. This doc is an experiment ledger: inputs -> scenario tables -> headcount trigger ladder -> pricing decay rules -> operational playbook.

Context and motivation: recent spike weeks have shown 48–72h surges that are expensive to satisfy via permanent hires or long-term slab commitments. We want a controllable short-duration buffer that product teams can request, with a transparent price signal that incentivizes quick de-escalation and usage optimization. The surcharge is designed to be visible to teams and to feed into chargebacks when above baseline.

Assumptions: baseline committed capacity (monthly) covers 90% of median request rate. Buffer pool target 60k reserved token-equivalent per sprint (2 weeks) for Q1-type workloads. Average cost per buffer token at current GPU mix = $0.004. Operational handling cost per buffer allocation request ~0.5 FTE-hours. Pricing elasticity baseline: short-term surcharge reduces 7-day token consumption by estimated 12% (hypothesis).

Experiment timeframe: Dec 1 2025 sprint -> Jan 31 2026 (three sprints). Success signals: reduced emergency hiring, lower unplanned spot spend, predictable activation patterns, <2% SLA incidents due to throttling.

Notes on fairness and credits: for enterprise customers with committed plans we apply a capped surcharge and separate refund/credit rules; smaller product teams will see full surcharge in internal chargeback.

Quick formulas: surcharge_price = base_unit_cost * (1 + S) where S = min(0.35, 0.15 + 0.20*(buffer_utilization_peak/0.8)). Decay rule applied per sprint-day d (0-indexed): S_d = S_initial * (1 - 0.15*d). Example: initial S=0.30 -> day1 0.255 -> day5 ~0.1275.
table_rows: Scenario,Buffer size (tokens),Peak util%,Estimated surcharge S_initial,Daily decay%
headcount_triggers: Trigger A: sustained >72h buffer utilization >75% -> open 0.5 FTE short-term contractor (3 month) request
Trigger B: 2 sequential sprints with avg buffer utilization >60% -> escalate to hiring review for 1.0 FTE Engineer/Infra
Trigger C: frequent day-of requests (>5 separate activations in sprint) -> require product-level optimization review, no hire immediately
Trigger D: SLA incidents attributable to throttling -> emergency hiring hold + immediate reserved capacity purchase (finance approval required)
pricing_sensitivity_findings: Pre-launch simulation: raising S by 10ppt reduced peak allocations in scenario model by ~9% (elasticity ~0.9)
Early pilot (internal teams): observed ~6% reduction in aggregate token usage when surcharge communicated with optimization playbook
Price visibility (dashboarding) had outsized effect; simply showing projected surcharge to teams reduced speculative burst activity
Caveat: enterprise customers with pass-through billing show lower responsiveness; treat separately with cap and credit rules

(S2) Instrument dashboard widget for per-team buffer utilization and projected surcharge - owner: Marco - due 2025-12-05
(S3) Run three-sprint pilot with Default scenario and capture telemetry (util, #activations, downstream spot spend) - owner: Liam - start 2025-12-01
(S4) Draft customer-facing note for enterprise contacts describing cap/credit rules - owner: Sofia - due 2025-11-28
(S5) Create chargeback ticket template and automation for internal billing - owner: FinanceOps - due 2026-01-10
(S6) Review hiring triggers after pilot and decide on contractor vs perm hires - owner: People Ops + Finance - review 2026-02-10
open_questions: Q1: What is an acceptable admin lead time for approving buffer requests during high-demand weeks?
Q2: Should internal infra teams get a discounted surcharge or separate buffer pool?
Q3: How do we treat multi-region activations where GPU mix and unit cost differ materially?
Q4: What guardrails should we add to avoid gaming (teams repeatedly allocating small buffers to avoid larger commit)?
